api:
OV.Data (js/data/units.js):
- soldierName(rng, natId, female, taken?) → string. taken(name) → bool is optional. Without it the function draws exactly as before (2 numbers). With it, a name that is already taken is drawn again, up to 8 times at 2 numbers each. If it still collides, the name gets the suffix " II", " III", and so on.
- NEW soldierNamesTaken(soldiers, extra?) → (name) → bool. soldiers is a {id: soldier} map or an array; extra is optional extra names.
- deployments.dep_alien_base.artefacts = {alien_food:2, alien_entertainment:2, alien_surgery:1, examination_room:1, alien_reproduction:1}. Unknown items are caught by strategy.validate.

OV.TUNE (js/data/tuning.js):
- NEW NIGHT_LANDING_MONTHS 2, NIGHT_LANDING_DAY_MARGIN_S 3600, NIGHT_LANDING_MAX_S 57600.
- SCIENTIST_HIRE 30000 and ENGINEER_HIRE 25000 keep their values; they are now labelled «ours».

OV.Soldiers.generate and OV.Campaign.makeSoldier: a recruit never gets the name of a living soldier in G.soldiers.

OV.Battle (js/sim/battle/battle.js):
- mission.garrison? = {crew:[{type, rank, tier, outside}], leftovers:{itemId:n}, crashed}. normalizeMission keeps it only when it is present.
- create(): with a garrison it deploys exactly garrison.crew, with a crash roll only if M.crashed && !garrison.crashed. Without one it uses the crew table as before (same RNG order).
- NEW B.crew = [{id, type, rank, tier, outside}] for every alien spawned.
- debrief(B, ctx) → adds aliensLeft:[unitId] and leftOnField:{type:n}, both filled only when there is no win. On a win:
  - dep.artefacts are recovered in proportion to the intact DEVICE tiles (rounded half up);
  - M.garrison.leftovers are added to the recovered items.
- NEW garrisonAfter(B, deb) → {crew, leftovers, crashed} | null. It is null on a win. An empty crew means the site has only loot left.
- NEW crewRange(mission) → {min, max}: the exact garrison size, or else Data.deploymentRange.

OV.Campaign:
- startMission copies obj.garrison into mission.garrison for a UFO or an alien base.
- finishMission step 7: when there is no win at a UFO or alien base, it sets site.obj.garrison = Battle.garrisonAfter(B, deb) plus visits:n, then calls Missions.onSiteCleared.

OV.Missions:
- land(): in months below NIGHT_LANDING_MONTHS, a night landing on land sets groundLeftS = max(traj.groundS, the first daylight in 30-minute steps + 1 h), capped at 16 h.
- supplyAt() deletes alienBase.garrison.

State (contract §1.11 / §1.14): ufo.garrison? and alienBase.garrison? are plain JSON. They survive OV.Save; this is tested.
summary:
I fixed 4 of the 5 round-3 findings at the root and skipped 1 with a documented reason. The Node suite passes: `node tools/test.js --strict --i18n` gives 726 passed, 0 failed. The new regression file is `tools/tests/sim_persona_r3.test.js` (11 tests, under 1 s). `qa/campaign_flow_check.mjs` passed 127 checks with 0 failures. `qa/full_campaign.mjs` failed, for a reason outside my files (see open issues).

1. **Duplicate recruit names — fixed.** `Data.soldierName` takes an optional `taken` check and draws again on a clash, then adds « II», « III». It is used by `Soldiers.generate`, `Campaign.makeSoldier` and the quick-battle squad. Checked: 60 new campaigns and 30 quick squads have no duplicate names, and the « II»/« III» fallback works.

2. **Alien bases gave no artefacts — fixed.** A won alien-base assault now recovers 2 Alien Food, 2 Alien Entertainment, and 1 each of Alien Surgery, Examination Room and Alien Reproduction. The amount follows how many alien devices on the map are still intact, and each gives the usual points while unresearched. Tested with all devices intact, with the topics researched, and with every device destroyed.

3. **Abort-and-return farming (major) — fixed.** A UFO or alien base left without a win now keeps a `garrison`: the surviving aliens (type, rank, weapon tier, placement) plus the items left on the ground. The next visit deploys only those survivors and does not roll crash deaths again. A later win also collects the left-behind items. A Supply Ship landing at an alien base restores its full garrison. The persona's own `farm.js` used to give 25/26/35/30 points and 186–319 k$ of loot on every visit; it now gives 25 on the first visit and 0 after. Tests check that the crew after 1 kill is the original minus 1, that crew types and weapons match, that the left-behind items are collected on the win, and that the garrison survives save/load.

4. **Night landings in months 0–1 (major) — fixed by a different route than proposed.** The 24-seed sweep (10 soldiers, Veterano, month 0) shows landed Large Scouts are equally hard by day (92 % wins, 3.2 losses) and by night (92 %, 3.5). Almost every alien shot (116 of 117) hit a soldier lit by the bot's own very-lights or muzzle flashes. I tried cutting alien night sight to 14 tiles: it changed nothing measurable, so I reverted it, and the crew tables stay as they are. The root problem was that a UFO stayed on the ground only 2.8–12.5 h, so «Esperar pelo dia» usually found it gone. Now, in months 0–1, a UFO that lands at night stays until 1 h after daylight (at most 16 h). The test checks that the UFO lifts off in daylight and is still there when the UI's hourly dawn check fires.

5. **Hiring costs marked «orig» — skipped as a deliberate design decision, now documented.** With the original costs (60 000 / 50 000 $) the campaign bot won 7/24 Veterano campaigns, with 2 council defeats. With the current costs it won 12/24 with none. So I kept 30 000 / 25 000 $ as an «ours» pacing choice, explained in `tuning.js`, the contract's tuning table and DESIGN §22, and a test checks those labels.

Campaign bot with the final code, 240 days, seeds 1–12: Recruta 10/12 victories (11/12 in round 2), Veterano 7/12 (6/12 in round 2), and 5/12 on Veterano seeds 13–24. No council defeats. A 2-seed `--det --save-mid` run exits 0. The contract has a new section §11.10 and updated §1.11, §1.14 and §5.9; DESIGN §22 lists the round-3 deviations.

I changed no screens, so I took no new screenshots.
deviations: Night landings: I did not use the persona's proposed fixes (one rank fewer for the crew, or alien night sight about 14 tiles). In month 0 Veterano already uses the easier crew table. A 14-tile alien night sight, measured, changed nothing. Instead, a UFO that lands at night in months 0–1 now stays on the ground until 1 h after daylight, which makes «Esperar pelo dia» a real choice (DESIGN §22, CAMPAIGN_API §11.10).

Hiring costs: kept at 30 000 / 25 000 $ and relabelled «ours» instead of going back to the original 60 000 / 50 000 $. Reason: the bot won 7/24 Veterano campaigns with 2 council defeats at the original costs, against 12/24 with none. The persona offered this as an accepted alternative.

Abort farming: the dead aliens' gear and corpses are not placed back on the next map. They are kept as garrison.leftovers and added to the recovery on the win, which avoids placing items on a newly generated map.
B (battle state) gains a crew array for every battle, and the debrief result gains aliensLeft and leftOnField. Battle hashes change, but no test pins hash values.
open_issues: Not my files: qa/full_campaign.mjs fails with «batalha jogada» missing and then a council defeat. At the first night crash site the `craftArrived` handler (around line 543) checks the text for /Iniciar missão/; the popup now says «Iniciar a missão?», so the regex misses and the script presses «Regressar». The Skyranger flies home, no battle is ever played, and the council ends the run. Another agent's run at 05:33 (ui4/campaign/log.txt) fails the same way. Patch for the QA/UI owner: in `case 'craftArrived'` accept /Iniciar (a )?missão/, or press «Esperar pelo dia» and let the dawn re-prompt come, instead of falling back to popBtn('Regressar').

Patch for the UI fixer (js/ui/campaign_ui.js), so the briefing estimate uses the real garrison on a revisited site. Line ~1115: replace `const range = D().deploymentRange(M.deploymentId, M.difficulty, M.month);` with `const range = OV.Battle.crewRange ? OV.Battle.crewRange(mission) : D().deploymentRange(M.deploymentId, M.difficulty, M.month);`. Line ~1024: replace `range = M.deploymentId ? D().deploymentRange(M.deploymentId, M.difficulty, M.month) : null;` with `range = M.deploymentId ? (OV.Battle.crewRange ? OV.Battle.crewRange(mission) : D().deploymentRange(M.deploymentId, M.difficulty, M.month)) : null;`.

Patch for the UI fixer (js/ui/geo_ui.js crewEstimate, ~line 392): before the deploymentRange call, add `if (tg.obj && tg.obj.garrison && Array.isArray(tg.obj.garrison.crew)) return { min: tg.obj.garrison.crew.length, max: tg.obj.garrison.crew.length };`.

Text for the UI fixer (pt-PT.geoui.js and geo_ui.js ~line 1995): in months 0–1, with a landed UFO (G.month < OV.TUNE.NIGHT_LANDING_MONTHS and obj.status === 'landed'), «Esperar pelo dia» is now safe, because the UFO stays until 1 h after daylight. A new key such as 'geo.ev.arrived.night.safe' could say «… Esperar pelo dia (cerca de {t}) torna a missão bem mais fácil — nestes primeiros meses o OVNI fica no chão até amanhecer.» instead of «mas o OVNI pode descolar entretanto». The waitIsDefault comment ('o tempo no chão … não se conhece') still holds after month 1.
